speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative review. Since you mentioned shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty, I need to clarify the nature of these symptoms. On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate the intensity of the pain, and does it worsen when you touch or move your ear?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent tympanic membrane perforation with granulation tissue formation (likely due to chronic infection or foreign body irritation), evidenced by shooting pain on eating (tensor tympani reflex) and difficulty wearing earrings.
